payload.title: AI Builders Daily · 2026-06-12
payload.summary:
**Google’s agent era is getting a real control layer**; **Anthropic says containment, not just alignment, is what makes powerful agents shippable**; OpenAI’s Codex orbit keeps pulling talent in, while builders on X keep arguing about the last mile: closed-loop tooling, safer autonomy, and whether current agent stacks are actually pleasant to use.

**Google 把 agent 这事往“控制层”上推了一步**；**Anthropic 明说了，光靠模型听话不够，真要上线还得把爆炸半径卡死**；另一边，OpenAI 的 Codex 继续吸人，X 上的 builder 们也没闲着，讨论点很实在：闭环工具到底谁来做，自动化怎么别翻车，现在这批 agent 到底有没有顺手到能天天用。

sections.headline: **Google DeepMind’s Logan Kilpatrick** says the model is no longer the whole story, the agent harness is / **Google DeepMind** 的 **Logan Kilpatrick** 说，关键已不只是模型本身，而是 agent 的执行框架
sections.body:
On **Training Data**, **Logan Kilpatrick** described Google’s new agent push as a shift from **Gemini** being the shared layer across products to an agent harness, referred to in the conversation as **Antigravity**, becoming the new through line. He framed it as an ecosystem spanning an IDE, web experience, CLI, and SDK, with the same base harness also powering products like Search, the **Gemini** app, Cloud, and **AI Studio**.

在 **Training Data** 这期里，**Logan Kilpatrick** 把 Google 的新一轮 agent 推进讲得很直白：以前串起各产品的是 **Gemini**，现在往前顶的是一个 agent 执行框架，节目里提到它叫 **Antigravity**。按他的说法，这不是单点产品，而是一整套东西，包括 IDE、Web 端、CLI 和 SDK；更重要的是，同一套底层框架也会给 Search、**Gemini** app、Cloud 和 **AI Studio** 这些产品供能。

He also argued that Google is still in the "crawl" phase for most agentic product behavior, with the **Gemini** app closest to "walk." On business tradeoffs, he pushed back on the idea that success means maximizing time spent in products, saying the real goal is maximizing user outcomes even if that means fewer eyeballs. He also suggested the jump from SEO to generative or agent-led discovery may look less radical than people assume because the systems compound on each other.

他还判断，Google 大多数 agent 产品体验现在顶多算在“爬”阶段，离“走”最近的是 **Gemini** app。说到商业取舍，他明显不认同“把用户留得越久越成功”这套逻辑，反而强调目标应该是让用户更快拿到结果，哪怕这会减少停留时长。至于从 SEO 走向生成式、agent 驱动的分发，他的看法也没那么戏剧化：变化会很大，但未必像很多人现在想的那样断裂，因为这些系统本来就是叠在一起长出来的。

sections.headline: **Anthropic** says shipping stronger agents now hinges on containment and blast-radius control / **Anthropic** 说，更强的 agent 能不能上线，关键在隔离和爆炸半径控制
sections.body:
**Anthropic Engineering** argues that as **Claude** gets more access across products, the core deployment question is no longer just whether failures are likely, but how much damage a failure could do. The post breaks agent risk into three buckets: user misuse, model misbehavior, and external attackers. It also lays out three defensive layers: the model, the runtime environment, and the external content the agent can touch.

**Anthropic Engineering** 这篇文章的重点很硬：随着 **Claude** 在不同产品里拿到越来越多权限，问题早就不只是“会不会出错”，而是“出错一次能炸多大”。文中把风险拆成三类：用户自己乱来、模型自己跑偏、外部攻击者借工具或内容下手。对应的防线也分三层：模型本身、运行环境，以及 agent 能接触到的外部内容。

The post is especially strong on containment. Anthropic says human approval flows degrade in practice because users approve most prompts, so the company has leaned harder on sandboxes, virtual machines, filesystem boundaries, and egress controls. It points to different isolation patterns across **claude.ai**, **Claude Code**, and **Claude Cowork**, with the broader claim that powerful agents become deployable when the environment puts a hard cap on what they can reach, even if model safeguards are never perfect.

文章最有料的部分在“containment”。**Anthropic** 直说了，人盯人的审批流在现实里会疲劳，用户大多数时候都会点通过，所以他们越来越依赖沙箱、虚拟机、文件系统边界和出口控制这类硬隔离。文中还分别讲了 **claude.ai**、**Claude Code**、**Claude Cowork** 的隔离模式。核心意思很清楚：模型防线再强也不是百分百，真正让高能力 agent 变得可上线的，是环境层先把它能碰到的范围钉死。

sections.headline: Loopcraft is stacking loops for reliability and leverage / Loopcraft 拼的是把循环叠起来，先保稳，再放大杠杆
sections.body:
## On Loopcraft

One might argue the entire game of the next century is to be able to stack loops as effectively as possible. 

In the early days of each phase, it will be valuable to know when to go **DOWN** a loop when things go wrong (for reliability)… 

but it will probably be more valuable to know how to go **UP** a loop as models improve (for leverage).

If you don’t figure out how to do this, don’t be salty when you lose to those that do.

## 关于 Loopcraft

可以说，接下来一个世纪真正的游戏，就是看谁更会把一层层 loop 叠起来。

每个阶段刚开始的时候，出问题时知道什么时候往 **下** 走一层 loop，会很值钱（这是为了可靠性）。

但随着模型变强，更值钱的可能是知道怎么往 **上** 走一层 loop（这是为了杠杆）。

你要是没把这件事搞明白，就别等输给那些搞明白的人之后再不服气。

sections.headline: Swyx wants a vibecoding platform that actually closes the loop / Swyx 想要的不是更多工具，而是真能闭环的 vibecoding 平台
sections.body:
the #1 thing that is driving me to build my own vibecoding platform rn is that none of them - and i lov vercel, cloudflare, netlify etc - none of them really close the loop for you in terms of setting you on the right path with errors and pinging you when shit fails (shit always fails)  

there's way too much "webmaster" infra to setup for every single project and i just want to do it once and for all, instead i'm being asked to npx posthog wizard here and npx arize skills there and it all just needs to be swallowed up into One Thing.

现在最让我想自己做一个 vibecoding 平台的原因，就是现在这些平台都不行。不是说我不喜欢 **Vercel**、**Cloudflare**、**Netlify** 这些，而是它们没一个能真正帮你把闭环做完，比如报错时把你带回正确路径，或者东西挂了以后主动提醒你（东西总会挂的）。

每个项目都还得自己搭一堆“站长式”的基础设施，实在太烦了。我只想把这套事一次性搞定，不想这里跑个 `npx posthog wizard`，那里再来个 `npx arize skills`，这些零碎东西本来就该被吞进一个统一产品里。

sections.headline: Box survey says the heaviest AI adopters also plan to hire more / Box 的调研说，用 AI 最狠的公司反而更想扩招
sections.body:
At Box, we just surveyed 1,640 IT leaders across the US, Japan, and Europe about agentic AI adoption. Many standout findings, but a big one was that the companies that adopted AI the most are planning to grow headcount the most.

Obviously lots of ways you can read that data and variables mixed in, but it’s actually quite intuitive that the companies that become most productive want to (and are able to) reinvest back into the business to keep getting the gains going. 

The narrative of jobs being wiped out assumes that companies will take a fixed approach to what they want to be able for work on. What’s happening in practice is it’s causing companies to want to light up more engineering projects, sell to more customers, automate more processes to give time back, and more. That all leads to more work to be done by people.

在 **Box**，我们刚刚面向美国、日本和欧洲的 1,640 位 IT 负责人做了一个关于 agentic AI 采用情况的调研。里面有不少值得看的点，但有一个很扎眼：采用 AI 最多的公司，反而也是最计划增加 headcount 的公司。

当然，这组数据怎么解读都可以，里面也混着很多变量。但直觉上其实说得通：生产率提升最快的公司，会更愿意、也更有能力把收益再投回业务里，继续把优势滚下去。

“工作会被清空”的叙事，默认公司对自己要做的事情是固定不变的。现实里更常见的是，AI 让公司想开更多工程项目、卖给更多客户、自动化更多流程，把时间腾出来。这些变化最后都会变成新的人工工作量。

sections.headline: Garry argues a 12.3% eminence rate among gifted kids proves the filter works / Garry 说，天才儿童里 12.3% 走到顶尖位置，恰好说明筛选机制有效
sections.body:
The centerpiece stat is a self-own: she cites a 35-year study where 12.3% of 677 gifted kids reached "eminence" (full professor, Fortune 500 exec, federal judge) as proof the category is a lie. 

The general-population base rate for outcomes that rarefied is far worse, much closer to zero than double digit percentage. 12.3% is the selection mechanism working spectacularly.

最关键的那组数据简直是在自己打自己脸：她拿一项 35 年研究说事，里面 677 个 gifted kids 里有 12.3% 最后达到了“eminence”（正教授、**Fortune 500** 高管、联邦法官），却把这当成“这个分类是假的”证据。

可放到普通人总体里，这种级别结果的基准概率低得多，离零更近，不是什么两位数。12.3% 恰恰说明这套筛选机制效果强得离谱。
